record.original_question: Let A be a boundedly approximately contractible Banach algebra, and let J be a closed ideal of finite codimension in A. Must J have a bounded approximate identity, extending the known codimension-1 case?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a Banach algebra. A continuous derivation $D\colon A \to X$ into a Banach $A$-bimodule $X$ is called approximately inner if there is a net $(x_\alpha)$ in $X$ such that $D(a) = \lim_\alpha (a\cdot x_\alpha - x_\alpha\cdot a)$ for every $a \in A$, and is called boundedly approximately inner if such a net can additionally be chosen so that the net of inner derivations $a \mapsto a\cdot x_\alpha - x_\alpha\cdot a$ is uniformly bounded in norm. The Banach algebra $A$ is called boundedly approximately contractible if, for every Banach $A$-bimodule $X$, every continuous derivation $D\colon A \to X$ is boundedly approximately inner.

It is known that if $A$ is boundedly approximately contractible and $J$ is a closed two-sided ideal of $A$ of codimension $1$, then $J$ has a bounded approximate identity (i.e., there exists a net $(e_\alpha)$ in $J$, bounded in norm, such that $e_\alpha j \to j$ and $j e_\alpha \to j$ for every $j \in J$).

Question: If $A$ is a boundedly approximately contractible Banach algebra and $J$ is a closed two-sided ideal of $A$ of finite codimension, must $J$ have a bounded approximate identity?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not turn up an explicit resolution of the question for finite-codimensional closed ideals in boundedly approximately contractible Banach algebras. Related literature on bounded pseudo-amenability and inheritance of bounded approximate identities by ideals was found, but no source directly settling this generalization of the codimension-1 case was identified.

status_evidence.title: Bounded Pseudo-Amenability and Contractibility of Certain Banach Algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Studies inheritance of bounded pseudo-amenability by ideals possessing certain bounded approximate identities, but does not address finite-codimensional ideals in boundedly approximately contractible algebras.
status_evidence.claim: Related work on inheritance of approximate amenability by ideals; does not resolve the finite-codimension question.

status_evidence.title: On a question related to bounded approximate identities of ideals in Banach algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs an example of a Banach algebra A and a closed ideal I such that the multiplier algebra of I equals A but I has no bounded approximate identity.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates the general subtlety of when ideals possess bounded approximate identities, but does not directly resolve the finite-codimension question for boundedly approximately contractible algebras.
